premise: Triceratops and Brachiosaurus squelch through the mud puddle and leave deep footprints in its soft edge; they wait while the sun bakes the mud hard, and Triceratops wonders how long the prints will stay — "a very, very long time," says Brachiosaurus — so they go and make some more.
inspiration: The folk motif of leaving your mark, turned true: how a footprint in mud can last.
lesson: Small moments with a friend can last a long time.
learning: Footprints pressed into soft mud can dry hard in the sun and last a very long time.

en-US.title: Footprints in the Mud
en-US.text: {puddle:enter} {triceratops:enter} Triceratops {triceratops:go to puddle by trot} came trotting up to the mud puddle. {triceratops:face happy} "Squelchy!" In she stepped. {triceratops:live stomp} {puddle:live splash} {sfx:squelch} SQUELCH! When she stepped out, she looked back. {triceratops:face surprised} There were her footprints, pressed deep in the soft mud. Then {brachiosaurus:enter} Brachiosaurus came by, slow and heavy. {brachiosaurus:go to puddle} SQUELCH! went his foot, and he left a footprint as big as a nest. [curious] "Will they stay there?" wondered Triceratops. {brachiosaurus:live bend-down hold} Brachiosaurus lowered his long neck to look. "Let's wait and see." {canvas:sunshine 0.8} So they waited, while the sun shone warm and bright all afternoon. The mud round the puddle dried, and went hard as stone. {triceratops:pulse} Triceratops tapped it with her toe. Tock, tock. Hard! {triceratops:face happy} "How long will they stay?" she asked. {brachiosaurus:live bend-down resume} Brachiosaurus lifted his head up high and thought. {brachiosaurus:face happy} [warmly] "A very, very long time." {triceratops:hearts} Triceratops smiled. "Then let's make some more!" And side by side, squelch, squelch, {puddle:live splash} the two friends went splashing through the mud again.

es-ES.title: Huellas en el barro
es-ES.text: {puddle:enter} {triceratops:enter} Triceratops {triceratops:go to puddle by trot} llegó trotando hasta el charco de barro. {triceratops:face happy} —¡Qué blandito! Y se metió dentro. {triceratops:live stomp} {puddle:live splash} {sfx:squelch} ¡CHOF! Al salir, miró hacia atrás. {triceratops:face surprised} Allí estaban sus huellas, bien hundidas en el barro blando. Entonces llegó {brachiosaurus:enter} Braquiosaurio, despacio y pesado. {brachiosaurus:go to puddle} ¡CHOOOF!, hizo su pata, y dejó una huella tan grande como un nido. [curious] —¿Se quedarán ahí? —preguntó Triceratops. {brachiosaurus:live bend-down hold} Braquiosaurio bajó su largo cuello para mirar. —Esperemos a ver. {canvas:sunshine 0.8} Y esperaron, mientras el sol calentaba toda la tarde. El barro de alrededor del charco se secó y se puso duro como una piedra. {triceratops:pulse} Triceratops lo tocó con la pata. Toc, toc. ¡Durísimo! {triceratops:face happy} —¿Cuánto tiempo durarán? —preguntó. {brachiosaurus:live bend-down resume} Braquiosaurio levantó la cabeza bien alto y se quedó pensando. {brachiosaurus:face happy} [warmly] —Muchísimo, muchísimo tiempo. {triceratops:hearts} Triceratops sonrió. —¡Pues vamos a hacer más! Y los dos amigos, uno al lado del otro, chof, chof, {puddle:live splash} volvieron a meterse en el barro.
